Chapter Details: Comparable indicators on energy, connectivity and data storage. 27 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
Value Name: Severe (frequent daily outages or regular load shedding)
revision_notes: Original 2015 World Bank Enterprise Survey source verified and confirmed accurate (8.2 outages/month for Ethiopian firms that year). Fresher and more authoritative evidence located: the Ethiopian Energy Outlook 2025 (Ministry of Water and Energy, Ethiopian Electric Power, Ethiopian Electric Utility and Petroleum & Energy Authority, May 2025), based on EEU smart-meter data, reports large users experiencing 39 interruptions per month with 21 hours of total outage duration. This is corroborated by the Energy for Growth Hub (December 2025), which cites the same 39 outages/21 hours per month figure, and by an IGC/RCT baseline survey (early 2026) of three-phase business customers in Addis Ababa/Sheger City finding an average of 23.7 outages per month (median 16). All sources indicate outage frequency has worsened, not improved, since 2015, and remains well above weekly frequency (roughly daily or near-daily). This supports retaining the top-severity code on the scale rather than reducing it. Value Code confirmed unchanged at 1 (Severe).
revised_comments: Ethiopia's electricity grid suffers from severe and frequent power outages that significantly disrupt businesses and households. Government data from the Ethiopian Energy Outlook 2025, compiled by the Ministry of Water and Energy together with Ethiopian Electric Power, Ethiopian Electric Utility and the Petroleum & Energy Authority, records an average of 39 interruptions per month for large (smart-metered) users, with a total outage duration of around 21 hours per month. Independent survey evidence from a 2025/26 randomised study of business customers in Addis Ababa and Sheger City similarly finds firms experiencing an average of 23.7 outages per month. These figures far exceed Ethiopia's own aspirational regulatory standards of 10-15 interruptions per year, and reflect outages occurring on a near-daily basis, consistent with regular load shedding and chronic underinvestment in grid maintenance and transmission capacity.
